title: Shapes & Solids
description: Class 1 IMO — Shapes & Solids: flat shapes, solid shapes, sides and corners, with olympiad reasoning and everyday-maths practice.

topics.title: Flat Shapes
topics.concept: Flat shapes are drawn on paper. The four we see most are the circle (round, no corners), the triangle (3 sides, 3 corners), the square (4 equal sides, 4 corners) and the rectangle (4 sides, 4 corners, with two long and two short sides).

examples.problem: How many corners does a triangle have?
Which shape is perfectly round with no corners?

recap: Circle: round, no sides, no corners.

quiz.q: How many sides does a square have?

quiz.explanation: A circle is round and has no corners.

topics.title: Solid Shapes
topics.concept: Solid shapes take up space — we can hold them. A cube is like a dice, a cuboid is like a brick, a sphere is like a ball, a cone is like an ice-cream cone, and a cylinder is like a tin or a pipe.

examples.problem: A ball is the shape of which solid?
An ice-cream cone is which solid shape?

recap: Cube = dice; cuboid = brick or box.
Sphere = ball; cone = ice-cream cone; cylinder = tin/pipe.
Solid shapes can roll, slide or stack.

quiz.q: A dice (used in games) is shaped like a ___ ?
quiz.explanation: A dice is a cube — all sides equal.
A sphere (ball) rolls because it is round.

topics.title: Sides, Corners and Shapes Around Us
topics.concept: The straight edges of a shape are its sides and the points where sides meet are its corners. We can spot shapes everywhere — a clock face is a circle, a window may be a rectangle, a slice of pizza looks like a triangle.

examples.problem: How many corners does a rectangle have?
A wall clock is usually which shape?

recap: Sides are the straight edges; corners are where they meet.
We can name everyday objects by their shapes.

quiz.q: How many corners does a triangle have?
A slice of pizza looks most like a ___ ?
quiz.explanation: A pizza slice has 3 corners — a triangle.

questions.q: Which shape is the odd one out:  circle, square, triangle, rectangle?
questions.explanation: Circle has no corners; the others all have corners.
The pattern alternates circle, triangle — next is a circle (●).

questions.q: A circle is to 'no corners' as a square is to ___ ?
How many sides does a triangle have?
How many corners does a square have?
Which shape has 4 sides but is not a square (two long, two short sides)?
questions.explanation: A rectangle has 4 sides with two long and two short.

questions.q: A brick is the shape of a ___ ?
Which object is shaped like a cylinder?
Which object is shaped like a sphere?
questions.explanation: A cricket ball is a sphere.

questions.q: A window in a house is most often which shape?
A shape has 3 sides and 3 corners. One side is then added to make 4 sides and 4 corners. Which two shapes are these?
Count all the corners of 2 triangles put together (not joined). How many corners in all?
